newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech ministers to discuss trade gap later today.
newsitem.headline: Czech ministers to discuss trade gap later today.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and other cabinet members will meet later today to discuss the country's growing trade deficit, government spokesman Ivo Strejcek said on Tuesday.

The discussion, which was originally scheduled for last week but was postponed because of a battle with the opposition over the first reading of the 1997 state budget in parliament, will begin at 1300 CET (1100 GMT), Strejcek said.

He said the focus of the meeting will be "foreign trade, agricultural foreign trade and the development of the balance of payments", but Strejcek said he did not know which cabinet members would attend.
The Czech trade deficit hit a record 100.9 billion crowns in the January-August period, nearly double the 59.5-billion crown shortfall in the same period last year.

After the release of these figures last month, the cabinet called on Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy, Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik, Agriculture Minister Josef Lux, central bank Governor Josef Tosovsky and head of the Czech Statistical Bureau Edvard Outrata to discuss remedies to the situation.
